extracted.intended_audience: Owners/operators of gasoline distribution bulk terminals, bulk plants, pipeline facilities; compliance officers; state/local regulators
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and compliance/reporting/testing/monitoring standards for owners/operators of gasoline distribution bulk terminals, bulk plants, and pipeline facilities under the EPA NESHAP subparts (leak detection and repair, storage tanks, loading racks, vapor control, monitoring, reporting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Leak repair and delay reporting (counts and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the total number and type of equipment for which leaks were repaired within 15 calendar days; the total number and type for which no repair attempt was made within 5 calendar days of identification; the total number and type placed on the delay of repair list; total leaks on the delay list at start and end of reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each leak on the delay-of-repair list during the reporting period, provide unique equipment identification, type of equipment, leak determination method (OGI, Method 21, or audio/visual/olfactory), reasons repair was not feasible within 15 days, and if applicable the date repair was completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gasoline storage vessel reporting per §63.423 / §60.115b
rubrics_metrics.description: For each gasoline storage vessel subject to §63.423, report the information specified in §60.115b(a) or (b) (or deviations per §60.115b(c)), or if applicable the info specified in §63.1066(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified reporting fields in the referenced sections depending on the control equipment installed.

rubrics_metrics.name: LEL monitoring deviation reporting for storage vessels
rubrics_metrics.description: If complying with §63.423(b)(2), for each deviation in LEL monitoring report: date and start/end times, storage vessel monitored, description of the monitoring event, wind speed at top of vessel, highest 5-minute rolling average reading, and whether the floating roof was repaired/replaced/taken out of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Description examples include concurrent monitoring with visual inspection, monitoring on a date other than required inspection, re-monitoring due to wind, or re-monitoring after repair. If floating roof repaired/replaced, also report re-monitoring info (dates/times/readings) for each re-monitoring done to confirm repair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of no deviations
rubrics_metrics.description: If there were no deviations from emission limitations, operating parameters, or work practice standards during the reporting period, provide a statement to that effect. If no continuous monitoring system was inoperable or out-of-control, state that as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A concise explicit statement in the semiannual report is acceptable when no deviations or CMS outages occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semiannual compliance report submission method (CEDRI/electronic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each owner/operator must submit semiannual compliance reports with required information to the Administrator per §63.13. Beginning May 8, 2027, or once the CEDRI template has been available for one year (whichever is later), submit all subsequent semiannual compliance reports using the CEDRI electronic template and procedures in §63.9(k), except mailed media must be sent to the Gasoline Distribution Sector Lead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CEDRI website will list template availability dates. Unless an alternate schedule is approved by the Administrator or delegated authority, reports must be submitted by the deadlines regardless of submission method.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA retained authority for alternative electronic reporting approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval of an alternative to any electronic reporting to the EPA required by this subpart cannot be delegated to State, local, or Tribal agencies; the EPA (Administrator) retains that approval authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §63.429(c)(5) for the non-delegable authority list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for gasoline dispensing-style tanks
rubrics_metrics.description: Gasoline storage tanks located at affected sources that are used only for dispensing gasoline consistent with tanks at a gasoline dispensing facility (as defined in §63.11132) are not subject to this subpart; they must comply with subpart CCCCCC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm tank function and the referenced definition to determine applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Throughput-trigger permanence
rubrics_metrics.description: If an affected source's throughput ever exceeds an applicable throughput threshold (definition of 'bulk gasoline terminal' or table 2 item 1), the source will remain subject to requirements for sources above the threshold even if throughput later falls below the threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarly, if a bulk gasoline plant's annual average throughput ever reaches/exceeds 4,000 gallons/day, it will remain subject to vapor balancing requirements even if throughput later falls below 4,000 gpd.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: covered emission sources
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart applies to gasoline storage tanks, gasoline loading racks, vapor collection-equipped gasoline cargo tanks, and equipment components in vapor or liquid gasoline service that meet criteria in tables 1–4 to the subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tables 1–4 to determine which specific pieces of equipment at a facility are covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance dates and phased applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance dates differ for new/reconstructed versus existing affected sources, with specific deadlines (e.g., new sources: upon startup if after Jan 10, 2008; existing sources: no later than Jan 10, 2011) and special phased dates for sources with construction/reconstruction on or before/after June 10, 2022 (dates vary, including May 8, 2027 and July 8, 2024 for certain provisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain requirements (listed in §63.11083(d) and (e)) have staggered compliance windows; consult §63.11083 to determine which specific items and dates apply to your source and which items are delayed until vessel emptying or specified future dates (e.g., May 8, 2034 for some items).

rubrics_metrics.name: General duty to minimize emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must at all times operate and maintain affected sources, control equipment, and monitoring equipment consistent with safety and good air pollution control practices for minimizing emissions. The duty does not require further efforts if applicable standard levels have been achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination of whether procedures are used may be based on monitoring results, review of O&M procedures and records, and inspections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational measures to avoid vapor releases
rubrics_metrics.description: You must not allow gasoline to be handled in a manner that would result in vapor releases to the atmosphere for extended periods. Measures include minimizing spills, cleaning up spills as expeditiously as practicable, covering open gasoline containers and storage tank fill-pipes with gasketed seals when not in use, and minimizing gasoline sent to open waste collection systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are illustrative measures — implement documented procedures consistent with minimizing vapor releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping and reporting for general duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must keep applicable records and submit reports as specified in §§63.11094 and 63.11095 (or specified cross-references in other sections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain records and submit reports on the schedules and in the formats required by the cited sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submerged filling requirement for bulk gasoline plants
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as specified in paragraph (b), load gasoline into storage tanks and cargo tanks at bulk gasoline plants only by utilizing submerged filling as defined in §63.11100, measured from the point in the opening of the submerged fill pipe that is the greatest distance from the bottom of the storage tank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submerged fill distances for different configurations are specified in the sub-section's paragraphs; confirm measurement point per the definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vapor balancing for plants ≥4,000 gpd (design & general requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bulk gasoline plants with an annual average gasoline throughput of 4,000 gallons/day or more must be equipped with vapor balance systems between fixed-roof storage tanks (other than those vented to closed vent/control device) and incoming/outgoing cargo tanks to capture and transfer displaced vapors. Lines must have vapor-tight fittings that automatically and immediately close upon disconnection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vapor balance systems must prevent vapors collected at one loading rack from passing to another loading rack; ensure system design prevents cross-transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vapor balance operational procedures and equipment limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must ensure procedures during all loading/unloading/storage operations: connect vapor balance during transfers; keep storage tank openings vapor-tight when not in use; pressure relief devices not open at tank pressure less than 18 inches water; cargo tank compartment hatch covers not opened during transfer; vapor balance systems prevent cargo tank gauge pressure >18 inches water or vacuum >6 inches water; pressure-vacuum relief valves in vapor balance system shall not begin to open below 18 inches water (pressure) or below 6 inches water (vacuum); do not transfer gasoline into cargo tank lacking current annual vapor-tightness certification per §60.502a(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are prescriptive operational and component-setpoint requirements — document operating procedures and verify cargo tank certifications annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small gasoline tank exception (<250 gallons)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gasoline storage tanks with capacity <250 gallons are not required to comply with the control requirements for submerged filling/vapor balancing in paragraph (a) but must comply with the requirements in §63.11085(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such small tanks must still implement the general duty measures to minimize vapor releases (see §63.11085(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Leak inspection requirement for bulk gasoline plants
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must perform leak inspections of all equipment in gasoline service and repair leaking equipment according to the requirements in §63.11089.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specific monthly/annual inspection schedules or alternative compliance options described in §63.11089.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial notification contents and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit an Initial Notification by May 9, 2008, or no later than 120 days after becoming subject (whichever later), unless meeting paragraph (g). The Initial Notification must include owner/operator name and address; physical location; a statement identifying applicable requirements in paragraphs (a),(b),(c) that apply; and a brief plant description including number of storage tanks in gasoline service, capacity of each, and average monthly gasoline throughput.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifications must be submitted to the applicable EPA Regional Office and delegated State authority per §63.13.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalency to §60.112b controls and LEL monitoring requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If a storage tank is subject to and complies with control requirements in §60.112b(a)(2),(3),(4), it is deemed in compliance with §63.11087. If subject to §60.112b(a)(1), lower explosive limit (LEL) monitoring per §63.11092(f)(1)(ii) must be conducted to demonstrate compliance; report this determination in the Notification of Compliance Status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph (f) of §63.11087 does not apply when demonstrating compliance under this paragraph (g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing and monitoring requirements for loading racks
rubrics_metrics.description: Gasoline loading racks at bulk gasoline terminals must comply with the applicable testing and monitoring requirements in §63.11092; as an alternative to pressure monitoring per §60.504a(d), one may comply with §63.11092(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify which monitoring approach the facility will use and document accordingly in compliance records/reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leak detection & repair (LDAR) program implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators at bulk gasoline terminals, bulk gasoline plants, pipeline breakout stations, or pipeline pumping stations must implement an LDAR program for all equipment in gasoline service according to either paragraph (b) (monthly inspections) or (c) (comply with §60.502a(j) exceptions) based on compliance dates in §63.11083.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the appropriate LDAR pathway and follow its frequency, method, and reporting requirements; the paragraph (b) monthly program is described explicitly below.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly leak inspection methods and frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform a monthly leak inspection of all equipment in gasoline service. Detection methods that incorporate sight, sound, and smell are acceptable for this inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monthly inspections must be documented in a logbook and signed at completion. Optical or instrument-based methods may be used but are not required under this monthly-sight-sound-smell route.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logbook and equipment inventory requirements for LDAR
rubrics_metrics.description: A logbook must be used and signed by the owner/operator at completion of each inspection. A section of the logbook must contain a list, summary description, or diagram(s) showing the location of all equipment in gasoline service at the facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each detection of liquid or vapor leak shall be recorded in the logbook, including dates and subsequent repair actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repair timing and initial attempt requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When a leak is detected, an initial attempt at repair must be made as soon as practicable, but no later than 5 calendar days after detection. Repair or replacement shall be completed within 15 calendar days after detection, except as provided for delay of repair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document repair attempts and completion dates in the logbook; failure to meet deadlines triggers reporting obligations and potential enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay of repair allowance and semiannual reporting of delays
rubrics_metrics.description: Delay of repair is allowed if repair is not feasible within 15 days. The owner/operator must provide in the semiannual report the reason(s) why repair was not feasible and the date each repair was completed for each delayed repair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the same unique equipment ID and description information as specified for delay-of-repair entries in the semiannual report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative LDAR compliance via §60.502a(j) (reduced frequencies)
rubrics_metrics.description: As an alternative to the monthly program, no later than applicable dates, comply with §60.502a(j) except: OGI monitoring frequency shall be annually rather than quarterly; Method 21 monitoring of pumps and valves annually rather than quarterly; monitoring of pressure relief devices annually and within 5 calendar days after pressure release rather than quarterly and within 5 days; pressure relief devices monitored only by non-plant personnel may be monitored after release the next time personnel onsite but no more than 30 days after release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When demonstrating compliance using this paragraph (c), the paragraph (b) monthly requirements do not apply. Ensure monitoring personnel and schedules conform to the relaxations and limitations specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance testing for vapor processing/collection systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct a performance test on vapor processing and collection systems as specified (e.g., paragraph (a)(1) options) except as provided in other paragraphs; performance tests must follow the conditions and methods referenced in the section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specific test methods and timelines in §63.11092(a) and referenced parts of 60 for method details and frequency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carbon adsorption device monitoring and records
rubrics_metrics.description: Carbon adsorption devices must be monitored as specified. Owners/operators shall document the maximum vacuum level observed on each carbon bed from each daily inspection and the maximum VOC concentration observed from each carbon bed on each monthly inspection, any activation of automated alarm/shutdown systems with a written log entry. The record shall include corrective actions taken, whether timely, and an estimate of amount of gasoline loaded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records should be in a logbook or other permanent form and include descriptions of corrective actions and timeliness per the monitoring and inspection plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thermal oxidation monitoring and alarm documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a thermal oxidation system is used, monitor operation as specified and document any activation of automated alarm or shutdown systems with a written entry; include description of corrective actions and whether actions were timely, plus an estimate of gasoline loaded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain written entries in a logbook or other permanent record documenting alarms and corrective actions consistent with carbon bed requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operate vapor processing within monitored operating parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Operate the vapor processing system so as not to exceed or go below the operating parameter values described in paragraph (b)(1). If an alternative parameter is approved, operate within that alternative operating parameter. Operation exceeding or going below the operating parameter constitutes a violation of the emission standard in §63.11088(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish and document operating parameter values from performance tests and monitoring plans; record excursions and corrective measures and understand they constitute violations if limits are not met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thermal oxidizer performance testing frequency and reuse conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: For bulk gasoline terminals using thermal oxidation, conduct a performance test no later than 180 days after becoming subject and at least once every 60 calendar months thereafter. A previous performance test may be used if it was conducted on or after May 8, 2022; no changes have been made to process/control device; operating conditions/test methods conform; combustion zone temperature recorded and usable to establish operating limit; and the test demonstrates compliance with the applicable emission limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure records of prior tests include temperature recordings and documentation showing no process/control changes to qualify for reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thermal oxidizer compliance options (CPMS or flare operation)
rubrics_metrics.description: For thermal oxidation systems, comply with either: (i) install/operate/maintain a CPMS to measure combustion zone temperature per §60.504a(a) and maintain the 3-hour rolling average combustion zone temperature at or above the operating limit during gasoline cargo tank loading at or above loads used to set the limit; or (ii) operate the thermal oxidation system in compliance with flare requirements in §60.502a(c)(3) and monitoring in §60.504a(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using CPMS, exclude periods with no liquid product being loaded; if excluding periods when cargo tanks other than gasoline cargo tanks are loaded, ensure exclusions were used when determining the operating limit per §60.503a(c)(8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flare monitoring systems requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For bulk gasoline terminals complying via flare emission limitations, install, operate, and maintain flare continuous parameter monitoring systems as specified in §60.504a(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the referenced section for the specific continuous parameter(s) to be monitored and required maintenance/QA.

rubrics_metrics.name: CEMS requirement for TOC and outage alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: For terminals complying via carbon adsorption, refrigerated condenser, or other vapor recovery systems, install, operate, and maintain a CEMS to measure total organic compounds (TOC) per §60.504a(b) and conduct performance evaluations per §60.503a(a) and (d). For CEMS outages, limited alternative monitoring methods per §60.504a(e) may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain CEMS per referenced procedures and document any use of alternative monitoring during outages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Floating roof inspection and LEL monitoring for tanks with internal floating roofs
rubrics_metrics.description: If storage tank has an internal floating roof, perform inspections per §60.113b(a) if complying with option 2(b) in table 1, or per §63.1063(c)(1) if complying with option 2(e). No later than dates in §63.11083, conduct LEL monitoring per §63.425(j). An LEL deviation is an inspection failure and must be remedied; repairs must be confirmed effective through re-monitoring and meeting levels in options 2(c) and 2(f) within the timeframes specified in §60.113b(a)(2) or §63.1063(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record inspection results, LEL readings, repairs, and re-monitoring confirmations as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: External floating roof inspection requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If storage tank has an external floating roof, perform inspections per §60.113b(b) if complying with option 2(d) in table 1, or per §63.1063(c)(2) if complying with option 2(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specific inspection frequencies and checklists in the referenced sections depending on the compliance option selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closed vent system/control device performance test requirement and control level
rubrics_metrics.description: If a storage tank is equipped with a closed vent system and control device, conduct a performance test and determine a monitored operating parameter in accordance with paragraphs (a) through (d) of §63.11092. The applicable level of control for such systems shall be a 95-percent reduction in inlet TOC levels rather than 80 mg/l of gasoline loaded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use performance test results to set monitored operating parameter values and document the 95% control requirement in records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual certification test for gasoline cargo tanks (Method 27 or railcar bubble test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual certification for gasoline cargo tanks must be via EPA Method 27 (pressure/vacuum tests: 5-minute period; initial pressure 460 mm (18 in) water gauge; initial vacuum 150 mm (6 in) water gauge; maximum allowable pressure/vacuum changes Δp, Δv of 3 inches water or less in 5 minutes) or via railcar bubble leak test procedures per cited 49 CFR requirements and ASTM/BS EN standards where applicable. No later than dates in §63.11083, updated maximum allowable pressure/vacuum changes may be as provided in column 3 of table 2 in §63.425(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Railcar alternative permitted only if railcar meets specified requirements and may not be used for any railcar that collects gasoline vapors from a vapor balance system that complies with a Federal/State/local/Tribal rule or permit. Use ASTM E515-95 (Reapproved 2000) or BS EN 1593:1999 for bubble leak tests where incorporated by reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative pressure monitoring methods during performance tests
rubrics_metrics.description: As an alternative to pressure monitoring requirements in §60.504a(d), you may comply with pressure monitoring requirements in §60.503(d) during any performance test/performance evaluation conducted under §63.11092(e) to demonstrate compliance with §60.502a(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the appropriate alternative per the performance test objectives and document the chosen monitoring method in performance test records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative conditions and recordkeeping for performance tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance tests must be conducted under Administrator-specified representative conditions (i.e., normal operating conditions) and shall include periods between cargo tank loading provided liquid product is being loaded for at least a portion of each 5-minute block of the test. Tests may not be conducted during malfunctions. The owner/operator must record process information necessary to document operating conditions during the test and include an explanation supporting that such conditions represent normal operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain process records, operating condition logs, and explanatory documentation with test reports to substantiate representativeness; exclude periods of malfunction from test datasets.
